FAST

TURIN, Nov 15 : World number one Alexander Zverev eased past debutant Rafael Jodar in straight sets on Sunday to score an opening group win at the start of the ATP Finals in Turin. The German, a two-time champion at the season-ending tournament of the top eight players, bagged a break in each set to clinch a 6-4 6-4 victory over the 20-year-old Spaniard, who has played a sensational first season on tour and has risen from the mid-100s to the top 10 in less than 12 months. Jodar, however, could do little to tame Zverev's booming serve and the most experienced ATP Finals player in the field, playing his 31st match, earned a break to go 4-3 up with a superb backhand down the line. The Spaniard had two rare break chances at 5-4 behind but could not convert either. Instead Zverev bagged the set in the next game and grabbed a break early in the second set to open up a 3-1 lead.

FAST

Nov 15 : Rory McIlroy secured a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title on Sunday, matching Colin Montgomerie's mark for the most Order of Merit victories in European Tour history before dedicating the achievement to his recovering father. The 37-year-old Northern Irishman carded a bogey-free 67 to seal a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai crown, edging Spain's Eugenio Chacarra in the season-long standings. Englishman Tyrrell Hatton, meanwhile, cruised to a five-shot victory at the DP World Tour Championship. The latest crown capped another fine year for McIlroy, who successfully defended his Masters title at Augusta National in April to secure a second green jacket and further cement his place among the game's greats.

"I don't really know what to say. Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up," McIlroy told Sky Sports. "I remember Monty (Montgomerie) being a stalwart of the European Tour. Going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years, I remember playing with him for the first time at the London Club on the European Tour in 2008. "To pull up alongside him and win eight of these things, it means the world to me. "I'm a proud European. I'm a proud European player and I'm proud to be a part of the DP World Tour and I'm very proud of myself right now." The milestone carried added emotional significance for McIlroy, whose father has spent the past two months recovering from major surgery. "He's been in the hospital for the last two months. He underwent a huge operation at the end of September, and he's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy said. "But when I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him before I went. He said to me: 'Go win the Race to Dubai.'"

Source: Reuters

FAST

BARCELONA, Nov 15 : Spanish second division team Tenerife returned to action on Sunday for the first time since the death of striker Jesus De Miguel, with emotional tributes before and during their game against Ceuta. De Miguel died on November 3, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a league match at home. Tributes took place around the country and on Sunday at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, Tenerife paid their own respects. A lengthy standing ovation bookended a minute of silence before the match. In the ninth minute play was stopped and a further round of applause followed, while a video of De Miguel was shown around the stadium, as occurred in all first and second tier games in Spain last weekend.

Tenerife fans also unfurled a banner reading "Jesus De Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white." Tenerife forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring in the 40th minute and he celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt to the crowd. Gil then revealed a message written under his shirt saying "Demi (De Miguel's nickname), always in our hearts." Neal Viereck added a second four minutes from time to seal a 2-0 win for Tenerife, ending a run of six games without a win. Tenerife are 14th in the Segunda standings, while Ceuta are bottom.  Last Saturday Tenerife's game with Granada was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel. The squad and staff were present at the Heliodoro and in Navahermosa three days earlier, where De Miguel was laid to rest.

item.title: Qualcomm employee laid off days before wedding; what his manager told him left him stunned
item.description: A Qualcomm employee in India has shared how his manager confirmed his layoff just days before his November 18 wedding. The incident comes as the US chipmaker begins a wider workforce reduction across its Indian operations.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Bhattacharya
item.content:encoded: A Qualcomm employee in India has shared his experience of learning that he had been selected for a layoff just days before his wedding. The employee, who was preparing to get married on 18 November, said he contacted his manager to find out whether he would be affected by the company's ongoing job cuts. What followed was an unexpected confirmation that he would lose his job.Qualcomm employee loses job days ahead of marriage, here's what his manager told himThe employee shared his experience in a Reddit post, explaining that he had already planned time off from 9 November to 24 November for his wedding and related preparations. However, reports of layoffs at Qualcomm left him worried about his position.According to the employee, he initially tried contacting his manager through Microsoft Teams and phone calls but did not receive a response. He eventually managed to speak to him and directly asked whether he had been selected for the workforce reduction.The manager reportedly confirmed that he was among the employees affected and apologised. The employee also claimed that his manager told him the company had originally planned to communicate the decision the following week, which would have been his wedding week.The employee said that while the news was difficult, knowing the outcome brought some relief because he no longer had to deal with the uncertainty. "Honestly, I am feeling more relaxed after hearing the news than I was before. At least the uncertainty is over, and I don't have to keep worrying about whether I will be impacted or not," he wrote. According to reports, the employee works as a software engineer, has spent around 4.5 years at Qualcomm and is based in Hyderabad. Qualcomm Layoffs: Another employee shares alleged severance details The wedding-related layoff account is among several employee experiences being shared online as Qualcomm begins implementing job cuts in India. In a separate Reddit post, another employee claiming to have been affected by the layoffs shared details of the severance package reportedly offered by the company. According to the employee, the package included three months' salary, along with an additional month's salary for every year of service. The employee also claimed that workers who signed their separation documents within two to three days would receive an additional month's pay. Other benefits reportedly included earned leave encashment, insurance coverage until 31 January and a bonus depending on the employee's team. The employee also claimed that affected workers would not receive their annual performance review ratings. However, these details come from individual employee accounts shared online. Qualcomm has not independently confirmed the specific severance calculations, payment conditions or signing deadlines mentioned in the posts. Why is Qualcomm laying off employees in India? The reported job cuts in India are part of a wider global restructuring exercise announced by Qualcomm chief executive Cristiano Amon in October 2026. According to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters, Amon described the exercise as a "performance-focused reduction" following the company's annual employee review process. Employee notifications were expected to begin in November. The company said the decisions would consider business priorities, organisational requirements and the skills needed to support its future growth. However, it did not disclose the total number of positions it planned to eliminate globally. Reuters reported that Qualcomm had approximately 52,000 employees worldwide as of September 2025.In India, reports suggest that around 1,000 to 1,500 employees could be affected by the restructuring. The cuts have reportedly started across Qualcomm's Bengaluru and Hyderabad operations, with other locations, including Chennai and Delhi-NCR, also expected to be affected.Qualcomm has around 18,000 to 20,000 employees in India, according to different media reports. The company has not officially confirmed the final number of job cuts in the country.The developments come at a time when Qualcomm is looking to expand beyond its traditional smartphone chip business into areas such as artificial intelligence, automotive technology and data centres.
item.wire:evidence: reporting reference, not an exact wire credit: Reuters reported

item.title: Por qué Chile dejaría de ser la cuarta economía de Sudamérica y podría ser superada por Perú en 2027
item.description: Perú podría superar a Chile y convertirse en la cuarta mayor economía de Sudamérica en 2027. El FMI proyecta que su PIB alcanzará los US$413.600 millones, impulsado por las exportaciones, la minería y ...
item.dc:creator: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — La buena dinámica de las exportaciones, los precios favorables de los metales y la estabilidad económica podrían llevar a Perú a superar a Chile y convertirse en la cuarta mayor economía de Sudamérica para 2027. Las proyecciones del Fondo Monetario Internacional apuntan a que el Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) de Perú llegaría a los US$413.600 millones en 2027, levemente por encima de los US$413.440 millones de Chile, según se desprende del World Economic Outlook (WEO), publicado en octubre por ese organismo. Ver más: Brasil y su “izquierda capitalista”: cómo Lula consolidó este modelo y qué retos tiene para mantenerlo Con ello, Perú podría saltar a la cuarta posición de las mayores economías de Sudamérica en 2027, por debajo de Colombia (US$634.700 millones), Argentina (US$762.290 millones) y Brasil (US$2,8 billones). Ya en 2028 la brecha se ampliaría puesto que el PIB de Perú llegaría a los US$434.970 millones y el de Chile a US$430.410 millones. La comparación se realiza en términos de dólares corrientes, por lo que el resultado final depende de otras variables como la inflación, el deflactor del PIB, el tipo de cambio y revisiones metodológicas de las cuentas nacionales. “El Perú cuenta con una base de crecimiento sólida, impulsada por sus fundamentos macroeconómicos, el dinamismo de la inversión privada y de las exportaciones, condiciones monetarias menos restrictivas y amplio programa de inversiones en diversos sectores económicos”, explica a Bloomberg Línea Mario Guerrero, economista y gerente de Estrategia de Inversiones de Scotiabank en ese país. “Chile enfrenta una expansión tendencial más moderada, con una dinámica aún débil de la inversión y menor dinamismo de la productividad”. Perú encuentra soporte en la minería, la agroexportación y la infraestructura, que son actividades que le otorgan al país andino ventajas frente a sus pares regionales. Por otra parte, Perú cuenta con una oferta exportadora importante de materias primas, especialmente minerales como el oro y el cobre, cuyos precios han aumentado considerablemente en los últimos años. Este escenario le ofrece margen para seguir creciendo en el sector minero, incluso frente a Chile. Los factores demográficos también influyen, dado que Perú tiene una población mayor. Además, la tasa de referencia peruana es una de las “más estables en el tiempo” y mantiene una correlación importante con la Reserva Federal (Fed, por sus siglas en inglés), expresó a Bloomberg Línea el economista de Pacífico Business School en Perú, Jimmy Astocóndor. “Lo mismo ocurre con nuestra moneda. Si revisamos la variación del tipo de cambio durante los últimos 25 años encontramos que su volatilidad ha sido prácticamente nula”, argumentó el economista peruano. “No hay otra economía latinoamericana en la que el dólar y su moneda local hayan mantenido una estabilidad similar. Esta es otra de nuestras fortalezas como país”. Sol peruano. Símbolo: PEN:CUR. Clase de activo: currency. Para 2026, el FMI estima que el PIB de Chile aún estará por encima y se ubicará en los US$402.240 millones, mientras que el de Perú en US$399.590 millones, según la proyección del WEO. “Todo pasa principalmente más por un tema de ritmo que de tamaño, ya que hoy ambas economías están muy parejas, en torno a los US$400.000 millones. El FMI proyecta que Perú crece cerca de 3% mientras Chile avanza apenas 0,6% este año”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea el analista chileno Renato Campos, CEO de la firma financiera Greyhound Trading. Detrás de esta tendencia, dice que está el mayor dinamismo de la inversión en Perú, especialmente en minería y proyectos portuarios como Chancay, que refuerzan su conectividad. Según Campos, también influye el aumento de la producción de cobre peruano, frente a la caída de la chilena, así como el aplazamiento de proyectos en Chile por la incertidumbre sobre las políticas públicas y los costos laborales, en un contexto de creciente volatilidad política en la región. En todo caso, el PIB per cápita a precios corrientes en paridad de poder adquisitivo (PPA) sigue siendo más alto en Chile (US$37,010) que en Perú (US$20,240), de acuerdo con el FMI. Para 2027, el FMI proyecta que el PIB per cápita PPA en Chile subirá a US$38,970 y el de Perú a US$21,260. “Esto lo leo más como una alerta sobre el crecimiento de Chile que como una pérdida real de posición”, opinó el analista chileno. Ver más: Perú puede superar a Argentina y desafiar a Chile en el listado de las potencias exportadoras de 2026 Los economistas debaten ahora si Chile está en una recesión técnica desde que el PIB se contrajo 0,02% en el segundo trimestre frente a los tres meses anteriores, tras caer 0,25% en el primero. En septiembre pasado, la economía chilena creció apenas un 0,2 % frente al mismo mes del año pasado en medio de la contracción de la producción minera, según informó el Banco Central. El ministro de Hacienda de Chile, Jorge Quiroz, reconoció recientemente que la economía atraviesa una recesión técnica , aunque afirmó que la actividad se recuperará pronto gracias a las medidas para estimular la inversión, informó Bloomberg. “Se le puede llamar técnicamente una recesión, pero básicamente la economía ha enfrentado algunos shocks de oferta este año, principalmente por la fuerte caída de la producción de cobre”, dijo Quiroz en una entrevista desde su oficina en Santiago. “Pero si se observa el sector no cuprífero de la economía, se puede ver un fuerte crecimiento”. Desde una perspectiva económica, “Perú tiene posibilidades de alcanzar y superar a Chile”, dijo el economista de Pacífico Business School, Jimmy Astocóndor. La razón estructural más importante es la velocidad de crecimiento real, que en el caso del Perú es superior a la de Chile, lo que ha contribuido a cerrar las brechas. Scotiabank calcula que el crecimiento promedio de Chile durante el período prepandemia (2000-2019) fue de 3,8%, mientras que el Perú lo superó 1 punto porcentual en todo ese lapso con un ritmo de 4,8%. Este patrón se ha mantenido durante el periodo postpandemia 2022-2026, con un crecimiento promedio de Chile de solo 1,7%, mientras que el Perú alcanzó un crecimiento promedio de 2,5%. Sin embargo, Astocóndor manifestó que también existen debilidades que se deben considerar, como ocurre en otros países de Latinoamérica. En primer lugar, se refirió al reto de la institucionalidad. “Ambos países venimos de gobiernos de izquierda que han dado paso a gobiernos de derecha. A ello se suma el manejo de los gobiernos, la gestión presidencial y la corrupción, que constituyen factores muy importantes que nos afectan negativamente como país”. Asimismo, hay otros desafíos como el crecimiento de la informalidad, vinculado al bajo crecimiento del PIB. “Si bien crecer a una tasa de 3% es relevante, no resulta suficiente para reducir significativamente la pobreza. Para que un país alcance mayores niveles de desarrollo y reduzca la pobreza, necesita crecer por encima del 6%, algo que no ocurre desde hace muchos años”. Por ello, considera que el fortalecimiento institucional, la mejora de la gestión política a nivel de gobernadores, un manejo económico adecuado y la presencia de buenos equipos técnicos en posiciones clave del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) son fundamentales. “Todos estos factores podrían generar un reposicionamiento económico de Perú frente a las principales economías de Latinoamérica”, según Jimmy Astocóndor. Entonces, ¿es viable que el Perú supere a Chile y se mantenga hacia el futuro? “Claro que es viable, pero hay varios aspectos que debemos atender”, anotó el analista de Pacífico Business School. En primer lugar, “el PIB debe continuar creciendo, pero necesita superar el 6%. Actualmente, existen alrededor de US$60.000 millones en proyectos peruanos que podrían impulsar el crecimiento económico por encima de ese nivel”. LEVI, Finland, Nov 15 : Brazil's Lucas Pinheiro Braathen won the men's World Cup slalom in Levi, Finland, on Sunday for his second victory in as many races this season. France's Clement Noel finished runner-up to Pinheiro Braathen, 0.56 seconds behind. Switzerland's Loic Meillard was third, 0.73 seconds off the pace. Starting seventh on the Levi Black course, Pinheiro Braathen led Noel by 0.65 seconds after the first run. The Brazilian skied a clean second run, giving up just nine hundredths of a second to the Frenchman. The former Norwegian racer, in his third winter competing for Brazil, has 10 World Cup victories, five of them in slalom, copying his win from last season in Levi.

Pinheiro Braathen, the Olympic giant slalom champion, also beat Meillard in last month's season opener in Soelden, Austria. "It’s rather emotional looking back one year ago in this very place where we won the first Brazilian World Cup victory in ski racing," Pinheiro Braathen said. "I'm just trying to make myself my biggest competitor and focus on the tasks at hand, the things that I’m working on in training," he added. "It is when I'm able to feel that I am having a lot of fun when I'm skiing, that I know that I'm letting go. And that's what it felt like today. Just a lot of fun." Noel will have another chance to beat Pinheiro Braathen in next Sunday's World Cup slalom in Gurgl, Austria. "The hill is different and we all know that there's going to be a lot of contenders," Noel said. "I will just try to focus on myself, ski fast and bring the confidence from Levi to Gurgl." Germany's Emma Aicher claimed the first women's World Cup slalom of the season on Saturday at the same venue.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 15 : Cristiano Ronaldo Jr was watched by a number of senior internationals as he made his Portugal Under-17 debut on Thursday, playing the final 20 minutes of a 4-0 European Championship qualifying win over Andorra. Vitinha, Ruben Neves, Goncalo Ramos and Joao Felix were among those in attendance at the Portuguese FA's Cidade do Futebol complex in Oeiras, on the outskirts of Lisbon, before their own training session. For the 16-year-old Al Nassr forward, known as Cristianinho, it was another step up the international ladder — and a debut that came at a moment of changing generations. Coach Filipe Ramos named him in his 23-player squad on November 2, three days before his father retired from international football.

The eldest son of Portugal's former captain made his Under-15 debut in 2025 before progressing to the Under-16s, collecting 13 appearances across those two age groups. Portugal next host Bulgaria and Serbia in the first qualifying round for the 2027 Under-17 European Championship, with the top two teams advancing. All their matches will take place at Cidade do Futebol. His name ensures scrutiny, but his father has long balanced ambition for his son with an acknowledgement that a famous pedigree offers no guarantee of success.  "Obviously, I'd love for Cristiano Junior to become a footballer and a top-class player like his father," Ronaldo said in 2016, when his son was six.  REMARKABLE CAREER Two years later, Ronaldo said in an interview with DAZN that he saw some of the traits that have driven his remarkable career in his son's game.  "He's very competitive, he's just like I was when I was little. He doesn't like to lose. He'll turn out just like me - I'm 100 per cent sure of that," he said.  "I enjoy teaching him a few things, but he'll become whatever he wants to be, and I'll always support him."  Portugal won the Under-16 Vlatko Markovic tournament in Croatia in 2025, with Cristianinho mimicking his father's trademark celebration after scoring in a 3-0 semi-final win over Wales.  The teenager spent time in the youth ranks of Juventus and Manchester United before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2023.  Both now play for Al Nassr, albeit at different levels, with Cristianinho scoring three goals in seven youth matches this season.

Source: Reuters

FAST

BEIJING/HONG KONG: Hong Kong property developer New World Development on Sunday (Nov 15) proposed a rights issue to raise about HK$24.9 billion (US$3.17 billion), a company filing showed. New World Development has been trying to cut debt, dispose of assets and bolster liquidity amid tight credit conditions and a weak property market. The plan offers shareholders 11 rights shares for every existing share at HK$0.90 each, representing a 26.9 per cent discount to the theoretical ex-rights price of HK$1.23 per share. The subscription price also represents an 81.5 per cent discount to the last closing price.

Controlling shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises (CTFE), which owns about 45.3 per cent of the company, has committed to take up its full entitlement and fully underwrite the remaining shares. The maximum CTFE commitment is about HK$18.7 billion. A CTFE statement said it supports New World Development resuming dividend payments when its financial performance and liquidity permit. The company plans to use about 34 per cent of the proceeds to prepay 10 per cent of about HK$82 billion in bank loans and extend the maturity of the remaining 90 per cent by two years. It plans to use another third to repay debt, including senior notes and deferred distribution of its perpetual securities. After the rights issue, New World's net debt to total equity ratio will drop to 48.3 per cent from 68.3 per cent. The developer aims to reduce total debt by between HK$40 billion and HK$50 billion by the end of 2031 to HK$93 billion to HK$103 billion New World's shares will resume trading on Monday after being suspended on Friday pending the announcement.

Source: Reuters/dy

item.description: America’s aging population is driving rapid growth in demand for home care workers, but many of those jobs still offer wages too low to support a family. Ai-jen Poo of the National Domestic Workers Alliance says the country will need hundreds of thousands of additional home care workers in the coming decades, while Harvard economist Lawrence Katz argues that expanding the workforce will not be enough if those jobs offer little opportunity for workers to move up. Three ships struck by drones in Black Sea near Romanian shipping canal, PM says

Reuters

15 November, 2026 06:30 pm IST

BUCHAREST, Nov 15 (Reuters) – Drones have struck three commercial ships in the Black Sea near Romania’s Sulina canal, Prime Minister Luca Niculescu said on Sunday, adding that his armed forces had scrambled fighter jets twice.

Defence Minister Stefan Radu Oprea said there were no casualties and that the ships’ crews had managed to control the fires on board after the strikes late on Saturday.

A growing series of deadly strikes on merchant ships near NATO members Romania and Bulgaria shows how the escalating maritime war between Russia and Ukraine is expanding into a major challenge for the transatlantic alliance in the Black Sea.

Show Full Article

The Sulina canal is a key Romanian shipping lane which links the Danube river to the Black Sea and is used by Ukraine for exports.

Romanian officials did not identify the origin of the drones but said they were a direct consequence of Russia’s war in Ukraine.

“These incidents are unacceptable and constitute a violation of international law,” Niculescu said. “They reflect the deteriorating security situation caused by Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.”

Russia has denied targeting Ukraine’s neighbours with drones.

Oprea said the three struck ships were Greek-flagged oil and chemical tanker Evia Petrol V, bulk carrier Marsol and oil products tanker Ali Najafov, both under the flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

Evia Petrol V and Marsol were struck 4 and 5 nautical miles southeast of the Sulina canal, the defence ministry said, inside Romanian territorial waters.

Oprea said a separate general cargo ship was hit by a drone late on Friday, also with no casualties. Private television station Digi24 said the vessel was Palau-flagged general cargo ship Larissa 1.

“On Tuesday and Wednesday I will be in Brussels for the meeting with my fellow (defence) ministers,” Oprea said.

“We need the solidarity of our allies, shown through patrols with surveillance aircraft and through equipment for counter-drone warfare.”

France temporarily relocated the Atlantique 2 maritime patrols aircraft to Romania after it asked for reinforcement.

Many of the ships hit in October and November were anchored near or sailing to or from the Sulina canal.

(Reporting by Luiza Ilie, Editing by Andrew Cawthorne)

FAST

Nov 15 : England opener Tom Banton struck a superb century and fast bowler Gus Atkinson claimed four wickets as they beat Australia by 135 runs in the second One-Day International in Adelaide on Sunday to level the three-match series at 1-1. Australia won the toss and elected to bowl, but Banton set the tone for England's imposing total by taking the attack to the hosts from the outset. The right-hander reached the second ODI century of his career from just 86 balls before finishing with 121 off 99 deliveries, including 12 fours and four sixes. After England lost Ben Duckett with the score at 19-1, Banton and Joe Root (62) rebuilt the innings with a 137-run second-wicket partnership, the highest stand for that wicket by an England pair in a 50-over match on Australian soil. Australia briefly worked their way back into the contest with three wickets in the middle overs, but wicketkeeper-batter Jordan Cox counterattacked with 67 off 49 deliveries and all-rounder Will Jacks struck an unbeaten 54 from 40 balls to propel England to 355-6, their highest ODI total on Australian soil.

Xavier Bartlett was the pick of Australia's bowlers with figures of 3-72. Set 356 to win, Australia slumped to 29-4 after Atkinson ripped through the top order. Matt Renshaw (63) and Cameron Green (64) mounted a spirited fightback to keep Australia in contention, but spinner Liam Dawson removed both batters to extinguish the home side's hopes. Australia's lower order offered some late resistance through Jack Edwards (17), Adam Zampa (18), Spencer Johnson (14) and Riley Meredith (17 not out), but they were eventually bowled out for 220. "We obviously bowled first thinking there might have been a little bit in the wicket, which probably sounds weird to say at the Adelaide Oval, and try to maximise those early overs," Australia captain Mitch Marsh said at the presentation. "I thought they batted really well. We tried a lot through the 50 overs, a few different plans with Meredith bowling bumpers, and all sorts of stuff. "Credit to England. They played well. We know they are a good side. A really rounded side and they showed that tonight." England's attack maintained the pressure throughout, with Atkinson finishing with outstanding figures of 4-28. Dawson and all-rounder Sam Curran chipped in with two wickets apiece as the tourists wrapped up a comprehensive victory. "The whole innings, we looked like we were in control," England captain Harry Brook said. "We countered their bad balls, put them under pressure when we needed to and Banton played an exceptional innings... "The depth that we have means we were able to go on and get that 350." Australia had won the opening ODI in Perth by seven wickets, with the series now set for a decider in Hobart on Wednesday.

Source: Reuters

Battle for young male voters intensifies after US midterm rebuke of Republicans

Reuters

15 November, 2026 05:00 pm IST

Follow Us:

-->

X

By Nathan Layne Nov 15 (Reuters) – Barely a week after the midterm elections, Democrats are debating how to turn newfound support among young men into a lasting coalition, while Republicans are trying to understand why the group abandoned them so decisively.

An estimated 59% of men ages 18 to 29 voted for Democratic US House of Representatives candidates, compared with 37% for Republicans, according to Tufts University’s Center for Information & Research on Civic Learning and Engagement. That marked a sharp reversal from 2024, when AP VoteCast found young men backing President Donald Trump over Democratic nominee Kamala Harris by 14 points, 56% to 42%.

That rapid shift has made young men one of the most influential and unpredictable voting blocs in American politics, with both parties viewing them as critical to winning the White House in 2028.

Show Full Article

Democratic Party operatives are wasting no time looking for ways to sustain their gains. At a conference on the party’s future in Denver last week, one session examined strategy for winning over younger voters, under the title: “What we are still getting wrong about Gen Z.”

Republicans have yet to conduct a formal postmortem, but party strategists and activists are already calling for an end to the unpopular war in Iran and measures to bring down the cost of living, according to interviews with five party officials and strategists.

“No party owns them,” said John Della Volpe, director of polling at Harvard Kennedy School’s Institute of Politics, arguing Democrats could keep some, if not all, of their gains if they deliver tangible policy results. “It will clearly swing.”

Economic anxiety was a major factor in young voters’ shift toward Democrats, but foreign policy also played a role, according to the Tufts post-election survey that found young men were more likely than young women to cite the war in Iran as an important issue heading into Election Day.

Trump’s decision to strike Iran not only drove up gasoline prices but also broke a 2024 campaign pledge to avoid new wars, a message that had resonated with young men.

Hours after the Republican rout on November 3, Vice President JD Vance, a potential 2028 contender who has cultivated support among younger voters through his opposition to foreign conflicts, blamed Trump’s decision to go to war for the party’s losses. Trump, however, continues to defend his decision, with no end to the war in sight.

One Republican Party official involved in national midterm strategy described the results as “a punishment election rather than a political realignment,” and predicted young men would return to the party.

A strategist who worked on a losing House campaign said Republicans could try to win them back by blaming future economic setbacks on Democratic overreach in Congress, including regulations that stifle growth.

The restlessness of young American men reflects a broader pattern emerging in democracies around the world. In countries ranging from France to Serbia, young voters have played a leading role in movements challenging the political status quo and protesting economic conditions.

CJ Pearson, a 24-year-old conservative activist who visited fraternity houses at Southern college campuses in the run-up to the election to try to rally young men behind Republican candidates, said the path to winning them back was simple.

“End the war in Iran. Bring down costs. And the coalition will return,” he wrote last week on X, describing the effort to regain young men’s support as “existential for the survival of our party in 2028.”

WINNING BACK THE ‘MANOSPHERE’

Trump’s appeal to young men in 2024 went beyond concerns about the economy and persistent inflation under former Democratic President Joe Biden. He used social media memes to cultivate a more masculine image than his opponent and appeared on a series of podcasts popular with young men, tapping into the online influencer network known as the “manosphere.”

Yet some of the same figures who helped Trump reach young male voters in 2024, including podcasters Joe Rogan and Theo Von, later criticized his administration over the Iran war and other issues, undermining his standing among their audiences.

Several Democratic candidates, meanwhile, turned to long-form podcasts, using less-scripted conversations to project confidence and authenticity and address a perceived weakness from past cycles, Harvard’s Della Volpe said. They also sought to recast a positive vision of masculinity as standing up for ordinary people and taking on corruption.

Della Volpe, a left-leaning pollster who studies young voters, cited Senator-elect James Talarico of Texas as an example of a new crop of Democratic leaders whose conception of strength rests on empathy and concern for the vulnerable. Those qualities, Della Volpe said, are frequently cited by the young voters he speaks with as important.

But above all, young men this cycle were looking for leaders who spoke to their economic concerns. That message was central to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s successful Senate campaign in Michigan. El-Sayed, 42, appealed to young men anxious about the cost of living and their economic prospects while also cultivating an image of physical strength, often appearing in fitted black T-shirts.

Milo Slevin, a 20-year-old who helped oversee El-Sayed’s outreach efforts on Michigan college campuses, said Democrats now need to show young people they are taking concrete steps to address their concerns, including by advancing the debate over universal healthcare, a core El-Sayed campaign pledge.

New York State Senator James Skoufis, who helped lead the Democratic National Committee’s effort to engage young voters this cycle, said ending Trump’s tariffs and lowering housing costs were among the tangible steps young voters would be looking for from Democrats in the new Congress.

“Young voters want more than just messaging. They want more than just talking points. They want deliverables,” Skoufis told Reuters.

Republicans, meanwhile, are scrambling to understand how they lost young men so badly. At a conference last week in Maryland hosted by the Heritage Foundation, a conservative think tank, one panel discussed the party’s challenge in winning back young men.

Veteran Republican pollster Kristen Soltis Anderson agrees with Democratic strategists on the need to get beyond messaging.

Republicans, she said, needed to offer young men “substance that says, ‘Here’s what we’re doing to make your life better, to help you form those families, to help you form those bonds, to help you buy that home, to help you have that opportunity.’”

(reporting by Nathan Layne, additional reporting by Tim Reid; Editing by Ross Colvin and Alistair Bell)

item.title: India invites Singapore universities to set up campuses, build townships
item.description: India has sought Singapore's expertise in developing university townships modelled on NUS's University Town, alongside deeper cooperation in education, research and innovation ...
item.dc:creator: Auhona Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: India has invited Singaporean universities to establish campuses in the country and sought Singapore's expertise in developing its proposed university townships, drawing on the National University of Singapore's (NUS) University Town model, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi said on Sunday. The proposals were discussed during Joshi's bilateral meeting with Singapore's Education Minister Desmond Lee at Singapore Management University (SMU), following the inauguration of the fourth Singapore-India Hackathon. In a post on X, Joshi said the two sides discussed strengthening cooperation across school education, higher education, skilling, research and innovation. “I invited more Singaporean universities to establish campuses in India and sought Singapore’s expertise in developing our proposed University Townships, drawing from the NUS University Town model,” Joshi said in his post. The invitation comes amid India's efforts to attract foreign universities under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. In 2022, the UGC had identified Singapore's leading institutions, including NUS, Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and Singapore Management University (SMU), among around 260 foreign universities shortlisted as potential partners for collaboration and campus expansion in India. Former UGC chairman M Jagadesh Kumar had said the commission would work with interested Singaporean institutions to facilitate their entry into India. However, none of the Singaporean universities features on the UGC's current list of foreign higher education institutions with campuses in India. Under the UGC's 2023 regulations, foreign universities can establish campuses in India, subject to eligibility and regulatory approvals. As of August 2026, the UGC had issued 16 letters of intent to 15 foreign institutions from Australia, Italy, the UK and the US. India's proposed university townships, meanwhile, were announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, which envisaged five such integrated academic zones near major industrial and logistics corridors. These are expected to bring together multiple universities, colleges, research institutions, skill centres and residential facilities. The Ministry of Education has initiated consultations with state governments, academic institutions and industry representatives to develop the framework. NUS's University Town is an integrated campus ecosystem that combines residential facilities, teaching infrastructure, study clusters and common spaces to encourage academic and social engagement. The two ministers also discussed mutual recognition of qualifications, deeper teacher and student exchanges, joint capacity-building programmes and stronger industry-academia linkages. “We also discussed collaboration in AI in education, advanced materials, clean energy, fintech, semiconductors and other emerging technologies, alongside joint research and support for deep-tech start-ups and innovators through Bharat Innovates,” Joshi said. Joshi also proposed hosting the fifth India-Singapore Hackathon in India in 2027 and establishing a periodic India-Singapore Higher Education Institutions Conference. The fourth edition of the hackathon, organised by SMU's Institute for Innovation and Entrepreneurship, the All India Council for Technical Education and the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell, is being held in Singapore from November 15 to 17, bringing together around 120 students from the two countries.

FAST

MANILA: The Singapore-Indonesia joint task force probing firms linked to haze-causing fires should expand to cover all Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) members, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Sunday (Nov 15). Speaking at the retreat session of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, Mr Wong said the task force – first announced in October – aims to improve coordination and information-sharing as both sides pursue those responsible for the fires. The task force "doesn’t have to be a bilateral platform", he said. "It should be an ASEAN-wide platform where we can share information more readily and where we can share evidence on those that are responsible, because fires can happen in any country in ASEAN, and we want to send a very clear message to all companies that this is not the way to go about clearing forests," he added.

"If anyone is caught doing this, across ASEAN, we will share information, we will take action, and we will hold companies responsible. I think that is something we should strive to do as part of ASEAN." The bloc already has mechanisms to achieve this, such as the Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution, which he hoped could be strengthened. Beyond extinguishing the fires, ASEAN must also work to prevent a recurrence, he said. Mr Wong also commended Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto for his efforts in investigating the cause of the fires and holding errant companies accountable. Singapore is doing the same with Singapore-based firms that may be responsible or linked to companies not upholding good practices in clearing forests, he added. Earlier this month, Singapore amended its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act to strengthen action against such firms. He thanked Mr Prabowo for "taking unprecedented efforts" to tackle the fires, which were worsened this year by climate change and a "very unusual El Nino season that resulted in a very dry spell". "I also want to express my appreciation for the many, many Indonesian emergency personnel and firefighters, who work tirelessly in very dangerous conditions," added Mr Wong. "We extend our deepest appreciation to them, and we send our best wishes for the recovery of those who are injured."

Related:

Singapore, Indonesia setting up joint task force to probe firms linked to forest fires; hotlines to manage differences

What should ASEAN focus on amid global uncertainty? PM Wong suggests 3 areas

Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim also raised the haze issue earlier in the summit’s plenary session. He said Malaysia has proposed Science Diplomacy and Sustainable Haze Fund initiatives through the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee framework, Malaysian news outlet the Star reported. Mr Anwar said the proposals aim to improve scientific collaboration, promote evidence-based decision-making and secure sustainable funding for the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Malaysia will push these priorities at the Conference of the Parties to the agreement next month and through its chairmanship of the steering committee next year, he added. REGIONAL TENSIONS Mr Wong also called on ASEAN members to work together to address border tensions between Thailand and Cambodia. "Singapore understands that this is a deeply emotive issue for the peoples of both countries. We would encourage both sides to continue exercising restraint, avoid escalation, and resolve differences through dialogue, including through established bilateral mechanisms," he said. Singapore will continue to support the process, especially as it takes on the chairmanship of the ASEAN Observer Team next year, he added. On Myanmar, Mr Wong said the bloc's member states have "a strong desire" to see the country "return to the ASEAN family in terms of its political participation" at some point. Engagement must be two-way, he said, with Myanmar showing "concrete actions that demonstrate real progress" in line with the Five-Point Consensus. This includes progress on humanitarian assistance, dialogue with stakeholders and the cessation of violence.

ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus

Following a 2021 military coup, ASEAN has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings as it has yet to make meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities. During a meeting in April 2021, all ASEAN leaders reached a consensus about the situation in Myanmar. The five points are: First, there shall be immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar and all parties shall exercise utmost restraint. Second, constructive dialogue among all parties concerned shall commence to seek a peaceful solution in the interests of the people. Third, a special envoy of the ASEAN chair shall facilitate mediation of the dialogue process, with the assistance of the secretary-general of ASEAN. Fourth, ASEAN shall provide humanitarian assistance through the AHA Centre. Fifth, the special envoy and delegation shall visit Myanmar to meet with all parties concerned. Source: Reuters

Collapse Expand

He acknowledged the Myanmar representative’s previous claim that not all violence is within the Myanmar government’s control, as some is committed by ethnic armed organisations. "We recognise that, but at the same time we also want to make sure that there should not be any violence committed by the Myanmar government, and there should be effort in terms of a sustained reduction of violence in Myanmar, as far as the government is concerned," Mr Wong said. Such steps would help restore stability in the country and build a long-term solution that is owned and led by Myanmar itself, ultimately benefiting its people, he said. "We would like to see that outcome eventually, but it takes two hands to clap," he said. "ASEAN can do more to engage, and Myanmar should also show its readiness to work constructively with ASEAN towards this goal. If we are united on both sides, hopefully we can see good progress on this."

By Joshua McElwee CHICLAYO, Peru, Nov 15 (Reuters) – Pope Leo will traverse the length of Peru on Sunday, the penultimate day of his South America tour, visiting a southern Andes Mountains city that was once the center of the Inca Empire and an eastern gateway to the Amazon rainforest.

Leo, the first Peruvian citizen to become pope, is on an emotional return to his adopted home and will travel 2,270 km (1,410 miles) in 12 hours for four events in Cusco, the Inca Empire’s capital, and Pucallpa, in the lowland Amazon jungle.

Church leaders hope the visits will allow more Peruvians to attend events with Leo, who has drawn the largest crowds of his papacy, some 12 million people across his 12-day, three-nation tour.

Show Full Article

They also think Leo might address illegal logging in the Amazon, where gold mining has cleared some 140,000 hectares (540 square miles) of rainforest since 1984 and poisoned regional waterways, according to a 2025 report from the group Monitoring of the Andean Amazon Project.

Leo, originally from Chicago, lived for about 20 years in Peru as a missionary and holds US and Peruvian citizenship.

He will start his travels on Sunday from Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023, and will end the day in Lima, before leaving for Rome on Monday.

In Cusco, Leo will also visit an archaeological site at the esplanade of Saqsaywaman, an ancient Inca fortress 3,700 meters (12,139 ft) above sea level whose stones were later used to build many of the city’s churches. The Inca Empire dominated western South America from about 1438 to 1533, when Spanish conquistadors toppled it.

Rev. Julio Velazco Paz, the Cusco archdiocese’s spokesperson, said the pope’s visit would highlight “the richness of our faith, our culture, our traditions.”

INDIGENOUS PEOPLE TO HIGHLIGHT LIVING CONDITIONS

In Pucallpa, home to the Shipibo-Konibo Indigenous people, locals hope Leo’s arrival will draw attention to poor living conditions.

“For us, the pope’s arrival is a source of great joy, but it is also a great opportunity to make our demands, our grievances, and our problems heard,” said Cecilio Soria, an Indigenous human rights activist.

Leo’s visit to high-altitude Cusco a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery has drawn some attention, as travellers visiting the city can experience altitude sickness.

The pope underwent surgery for lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer, on October 13. His doctors have said the cancer was localized and had not spread, and the pope will not require further treatment.

Medical experts have said the pope faces no special dangers on the trip, but may need to take rest breaks or use supplemental oxygen, as many travellers do.

Travelling to high altitude a few weeks after lung surgery is not unusual, said Dr. Stephen Cassivi, a professor of thoracic surgery at the Mayo Clinic, a nonprofit US medical center.

(Reporting by Joshua McElwee; additional reporting by Cassandra Garrison, Santiago Limachi, Fiorella Azaña, Leila Miller; editing by Rod Nickel)

item.title: Bitcoin falls to four-month low near $62K as crypto selloff deepens
item.description: Bitcoin fell to a four-month low near $62,000 on Sunday, extending a selloff across major digital assets before recovering some of its losses.On Sunday, Bitcoin BITSTAMP:BTCUSD dropped to a 24-hour ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Cointelegraph / Bitcoin falls to four-month low near $62K as crypto selloff deepens

Bitcoin falls to four-month low near $62K as crypto selloff deepens Less than 1 min read

BTCUSD ETHUSD SOLUSD Bitcoin fell to a four-month low near $62,000 on Sunday, extending a selloff across major digital assets before recovering some of its losses. On Sunday, Bitcoin BTCUSD dropped to a 24-hour low of $62,080.91, according to CoinGecko, its weakest level since July. The asset later rebounded above $65,000 but remained down nearly 15% in the last seven days. The downturn extended beyond Bitcoin. CoinGecko data showed Ether ETHUSD down 19.5% over the past week, while Solana SOLUSD lost 20.7%. The total value of the cryptocurrency market fell about 4% over 24 hours to $2.26 trillion, according to CoinGecko. Market sentiment also deteriorated. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to 10 on Sunday from 13 on Saturday and 20 on Friday, remaining in “extreme fear,” according to Alternative.me. The move followed Friday’s slide below $70,000, as analysts reported weakening investor sentiment and concerns over institutional outflows and tighter liquidity. The latest decline came after US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted $2.35 billion in net outflows over two consecutive weeks. The funds lost $1.07 billion during the week ended Nov. 13, following $1.28 billion the previous week. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust extended its outflow streak to 11 trading sessions on Friday.

FAST

Nov 15 : India pulled off a remarkable escape in Tauranga on Sunday, with Arshdeep Singh leading a pace-led fightback to secure a thrilling 22-run win over New Zealand and seal the five-match one-day international series 3-1. Defending a modest 209, India looked destined for defeat as New Zealand cruised to 64-1 before the visitors' pacers sparked a dramatic collapse, with the hosts losing five wickets for 55 runs before crashing out on 187 in 48.1 overs. Put in to bat, India made a cautious start, mindful of their crushing 244-run defeat in the previous ODI, but their approach unravelled as New Zealand's bowlers ripped through the top order before Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan helped the visitors recover to 209 all out in 42.1 overs. New Zealand openers Will Young and Nick Kelly capitalised on the platform laid by their bowlers and looked on course for a comfortable chase before India's bowlers breathed life into the contest in the middle overs, relentlessly attacking the stumps and denying the hosts any opportunity to counterattack.

Yash Thakur built pressure with a disciplined spell, while Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep struck at regular intervals as the hosts slumped from 64-1 to 119-6. Dean Foxcroft top-scored with 31 off 42 balls and attempted to steady the innings as wickets tumbled around him, but Yash removed him to claim his maiden ODI wicket. Captain Mitchell Santner's 24 off 31 balls offered resistance, but India's bowlers continued to chip away and eventually wrapped up the tail to complete a memorable victory. "We didn't have a great batting but our bowlers all bowled with the same direction and we were able to execute," said captain Shreyas Iyer, who backed his seamers for the bulk of the innings before turning to spin in the 36th over. "This whole series was not a good one for batters but the mindset is to take the team through irrespective of the conditions." Player of the Match Arshdeep finished with figures of 3-30, while Siraj and spinner Patel picked up two wickets apiece and the remaining bowlers claimed one each. "India bowled really well tonight," Santner said. "Shreyas did a great job rotating his seamers and holding Axar back. If we took each partnership a little longer, we would've won the game. It was a great bowling performance from India." Earlier, New Zealand's attack kept India on the back foot throughout, with fast bowler Matthew Fisher striking early to remove veterans Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. Patel, who survived two chances, stitched together a 52-run partnership with Shreyas (22) before combining with Kishan in a bid to rebuild the innings. Patel and Kishan scored 46 apiece, while Naman Dhir contributed a late 22 before Jacob Duffy and Santner wrapped up the tail. Santner (3-47) and Duffy (3-60) claimed three wickets each, while Fisher finished with two. India and New Zealand will next meet in a two-test series beginning on November 19.

Source: Reuters

Defence The FinePrint

Inside Pakistan’s air-to-air missile arsenal: From Chinese PL-15s to indigenous Fa’az

The Fa’az test marks a potential shift in Pakistan’s dependence on Chinese and American suppliers, even as imported missiles continue to form the backbone of its air combat inventory.

Bantirani Patro

15 November, 2026 03:14 pm IST

Follow Us:

-->

Facebook

X

LinkedIn

WhatsApp

Email

Copy Link

Illustration: Soham Sen/ThePrint

Stay updated with ThePrint:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

-->

New Delhi: Pakistan recently flight-tested its first indigenously developed air-to-air missile (AAM), named Fa’az (Urdu for victorious). The development marks a significant step for the country, which has so far relied primarily on Chinese- and US-made missiles. For India, the development merits attention, as recent standoffs between the two countries have been characterised by aerial engagements and Pakistan could potentially use the missile for a future conflict.

On 3 November, the day of the test, Pakistan military’s media wing, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), said, “The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defence industry.”

A video released by Pakistan showed the missile fitted onto a JF-17 Thunder, the fighter aircraft jointly developed by Pakistan and China.

Show Full Article

Equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system, Fa’az is designed to engage enemy aerial targets at longer ranges, placing it in the category of Beyond-Visual-Range Air-to-Air Missiles (BVRAAMs). Importantly, the missile shown in the video was the passive imaging infrared (IIR) version, known as Fa’az IIR. A separate active radar-guided (RF) variant is also under development.

IIR missiles are tactically more effective as they use thermal imaging to build a two-dimensional image or silhouette of the target before locking on, rather than relying primarily on the heat signature of the target as older infrared (IR) missiles do.

The Fa’az IIR has an estimated detection range of 40 kilometres, while the RF version has a detection range of 25 km. Both variants are projected to have a range exceeding 100 km and a maximum speed of Mach 3.5 (supersonic).

The missile is being developed under Pakistan’s National Engineering and Scientific Commission (NESCOM) by the state-owned defence conglomerate Global Industrial and Defence Solutions (GIDS). The company first showcased mock-ups of both Fa’az variants at a defence exhibition in Istanbul, Turkey, in 2023. GIDS maintains that its products are developed locally and that it owns their intellectual property rights.

Pakistan has not released detailed information about Fa’az’s flight test or disclosed the development status of its radar-guided RF variant. Regardless of when the missile enters operational service, the test marks a significant step for Pakistan’s air defence industry.

Writing for The War Zone , a defence and military analysis website, Thomas Newdick described it as “a significant development in the country’s efforts to establish a domestic air-to-air weapons capability and join a relatively small group of countries with the expertise to develop such weapons”.

Also Read: Why Pakistan’s veteran power broker Maulana Fazlur Rehman is now challenging the military

Moving beyond American and Chinese missiles Air Marshal Diptendu Choudhury (Retd), an airpower specialist and author affiliated with several Indian think-tanks, told ThePrint that Pakistan was dependent on the US for long, but started looking to China after America imposed sanctions on the sale of F-16s to Islamabad in 1990. “The Chinese helped Pakistan with technology, while Pakistan assisted the Chinese air force in expanding its operational experience by way of bilateral joint exercises like Shaheen.” He added that there were limits to the extent of China’s assistance, prompting Pakistan to move towards self-reliance.

Beyond reducing dependence on foreign suppliers, greater domestic production could also allow Pakistan to export its weapons systems. Fa’az could complement the JF-17 Thunder, which Pakistan is already exporting, giving prospective buyers the option of acquiring both the fighter aircraft and its accompanying air-to-air missile.

However, Air Marshal AK Bharti, Director General of Air Operations during Operation Sindoor, questioned Pakistan’s claim that the missile was indigenous. “The indigenous component of Fa’az should be taken with a pinch of salt, as they could very well just be assembling foreign components,” he told ThePrint.

Foreign technological influences in Pakistan’s indigenous missile inventory cannot be ruled out, given Islamabad’s longstanding defence ties with China. GIDS is also developing a longer-range missile, called Fa’az-2, in technological cooperation with Turkey’s TÜBİTAK SAGE, which is developing the country’s own air-to-air missile, GÖKDOĞAN.

Air Marshal Bharti said India should take note of the development regardless of how much of the missile is indigenous. “It is a capability with the adversary, however small it may be,” he said.

Recent clashes between India and Pakistan have predominantly involved beyond-visual-range (BVR) engagements. A defining feature of Operation Sindoor was that aircraft from neither India nor Pakistan crossed into each other’s airspace and the fighting occurred through long-range and BVR platforms.

“The next India-Pakistan standoff, as indeed an aerial battle anywhere in the world, would predominantly be a BVR combat, but you cannot do away with within-visual-range AAMs (WVRAAMs) completely,” Air Marshal Bharti told ThePrint.

Against this backdrop, it is important to take stock of the PAF’s existing BVRAAM inventory.

Illustration: Soham Sen/ThePrint PL-12/SD-10A Among the longer-range missiles in Pakistan’s inventory is the Chinese SD-10A BVRAAM, an export variant of the PL-12 missile. It is produced under licence by the Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and appears to have partly influenced Fa’az’s design.

A report by the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) said the PL-12 was China’s first indigenous active radar-guided air-to-air missile. It entered service with the Chinese Air Force and Navy in 2005.

The SD-10A is an active radar-guided BVRAAM fitted on Chinese combat aircraft, including the JF-17 Thunder. Its range is slightly lower than that of the PL-12 which, according to many estimates, has a maximum range of 100 km, with the export version having a maximum range of roughly 70 km.

PL-15E and Operation Sindoor Another long-range missile in Pakistan’s inventory is the Chinese PL-15E, the export variant of the PL-15. It is integrated into the armament of the J-10C and JF-17 Block III fighters.

Designed as an advanced successor to the PL-12, the PL-15 is equipped with an active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar seeker. It is powered by a dual-pulse solid rocket motor and has a maximum speed of Mach 4–5 (supersonic).

The RUSI report notes that the PL-15 has a profile visually similar to the US-made AIM-120 C/D Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), but “outranges the latest AIM-120D model and has a comparable maximum range to the Meteor [French-made missile]”.

Pakistan was the first export customer for the PL-15E. Its first deployment came during the May 2025 confrontation with India, following the Pahalgam attack. Missile debris reportedly fell inside Indian territory in Hoshiarpur, Punjab. Air Marshal AK Bharti subsequently confirmed at a press briefing following Operation Sindoor that Pakistan had used the missile, pointing to its debris.

The PL-15E’s operational range caught the Indian Air Force (IAF) off guard, according to a Reuters report. Indian officials had estimated its range at approximately 150 km. The missile, however, struck an Indian aircraft from a distance of nearly 200 km during combat, Reuters reported.

American AAMs Illustration: Soham Sen/ThePrint For its fleet of American F-16 Fighting Falcon aircraft, Pakistan relies on US-made AAMs, particularly the AIM-120C-5 AMRAAM. According to data from one of its operators, the AIM-120C-5 has a maximum range of around 74 km.

During the 2019 India-Pakistan confrontation following the Pulwama attack, India publicly displayed debris from an AIM-120C-5 as evidence that Pakistan had deployed its American-made F-16s against India.

“Pakistan claimed they did not use F-16. There is enough evidence to show that F-16s were used in this mission through their electronic signatures. Parts of AMRAAM air-to-air missile, which is carried only on the F-16s, was recovered east of Rajouri within Indian territory,” Air Vice Marshal R.G.K. Kapoor had said after the 2019 confrontation.

Air Marshal Diptendu Choudhury said the US had refused to acknowledge that Pakistan used F-16s against India, given Islamabad’s assurances that the aircraft would be used for counter-terrorism operations rather than against India.

Months after Operation Sindoor, the US confirmed the sale of AMRAAMs to Pakistan through defence manufacturer Raytheon. On 30 September 2025, the US Department of War issued a press release announcing contracts awarded to several American defence firms. The US Embassy in India subsequently confirmed the sale, but described it not as a new agreement to upgrade Pakistan’s existing capabilities, but as “an existing Foreign Military Sales contract for sustainment and spares for several countries, including Pakistan”.

Pakistan had earlier purchased 700 AAMs from US-based Raytheon in 2007. The order included 500 AMRAAMs, making it the largest international order for the weapon at the time, and 200 short-range AIM-9M Sidewinder missiles.

The bigger question here is whether Pakistan would deploy its American AMRAAM (and its F-16 fleet at large) against India again, even though the PAF’s large inventory of Chinese-AAMs provides enough alternatives to bypass American systems against India.

French and American short-range AAMs The infrared-guided Sidewinder remains a short-range weapon of choice for Pakistan’s F-16 fleet. The PAF continues to operate the all-aspect AIM-9L and the older AIM-9P variants.

It also operates the French-made, infrared-guided Matra Magic 2 AAM, which is comparable to the AIM-9L and offers an alternative to the US-made weapon.

These short-range AAMs (SRAAMs) are primarily intended for within-visual-range (WVR) dogfights. Given the changing nature of aerial combat and the growing importance of BVRAAMs, their role in a future India-Pakistan confrontation may be more limited.

Implications for India Air Marshal AK Bharti told ThePrint that India should take note of the development without being unduly alarmed. “Any new weapon the adversary gets will naturally be a cause of concern, but India need not be unduly alarmed by this development. Of course, India must continue to keep its eyes open and factor in each and every development across the border, in its larger scheme of things,” he said.

Given Pakistan’s asymmetry with India and its continued reliance on foreign suppliers, maintaining a substantial stockpile of AAMs remains critical for Islamabad. However, dependence on other countries poses both financial and geopolitical constraints and indigenous production could reduce the risk of the PAF depleting its BVRAAM supplies in the case of a prolonged conflict with India.

Air Marshal Choudhury said that, over and above the radar range, the missile’s range should be greater than the adversary’s. “India for the longest time, up until the Kargil war, had a BVR missile advantage over Pakistan. This advantage lay in the Indian Air Force’s AAM ability to outstick PAF’s.”

Put simply, the IAF’s missiles had a greater range than Pakistan’s weapons. By the 2019 Balakot strikes, however, Pakistan possessed more sophisticated AMRAAMs than India’s, the Air Marshal said.

India has its own indigenous BVRAAM family, Astra, developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). The Astra Mk-1, with a range exceeding 100 kilometres, has already been inducted into the IAF. Its range is being extended, while the Astra Mk-2 is undergoing testing. Plans are also underway for the Astra Mk-3.

So, while Fa’az expanded the weapons options available to its Air Force, what will ultimately matter is whether Pakistan can match or exceed Indian missile ranges and how quickly it can produce and induct the missile into operational service.

India remains ahead of Pakistan in indigenous AAM development and has demonstrated this through its Astra programme.

Air Marshal Choudhury said, “There is a long way till Pakistan inducts Fa’az into its service. Nevertheless, India should keep up the pace and accelerate its own missile technology. It’s a cat-and-mouse game in which India should remain ahead of Pakistan both in terms of weapons capability and scalability. India should also widen its choices on the AAMs menu and should continue upgrading its missiles by increasing their ranges, and making them lighter and smarter.”

(Edited by Chingkheinganbi Mayengbam)

FAST

Nov 15 : Former Australia test bowler Chadd Sayers backed Usman Khawaja's claims about the Sandpapergate scandal on Sunday, saying he believes everyone in the side during the 2018 tour of South Africa knew sandpaper was being used to alter the condition of the ball. The tampering, discovered during the third test at Newlands in Cape Town, led to former captain Steve Smith and vice captain David Warner being banned for 12 months by Cricket Australia (CA) from elite cricket. Cameron Bancroft received a nine-month suspension for his part in the incident. Khawaja wrote in his autobiography "Sabr: Finding my way in Cricket and Life", released on Tuesday, that knowledge of the plan was not limited to the three players who were punished and was more widespread within the team. In the wake of the new allegations, CA has ruled out reopening its 2018 investigation, while Warner has accused the sports body of orchestrating a cover-up by ignoring key witnesses and seeking to pin blame on three players.

"I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used," Sayers told SEN radio. Sayers, 39, also echoed Khawaja's claim that sandpaper was used during the second test at Port Elizabeth, saying he was the player who removed it from the field. "It (sandpaper) was given to me to take off, so that wasn't planned or anything. I was just the player who took the drinks out at the time ... it was passed on to me," he said. Sayers, who made his only test appearance for Australia in the fourth test of the 2018 South Africa tour, said he was never interviewed as part of CA's inquiry. He added that maybe it was because he was 12th man and didn't play in the game or perhaps because he knew too much information. "I'm not too sure," he said. Fast bowler Mitchell Starc denied any prior knowledge of the incident on Tuesday, while Australia captain Pat Cummins dismissed suggestions of his involvement, describing the allegations as "utter nonsense" on Friday. Sayers, however, said he is convinced the entire team, including the bowlers, knew what was happening. "When you're trying to get the ball to reverse, everyone has to buy in because if one little thing goes wrong in the field to the ball, it stops it from reversing straight away. I'm pretty confident to say that everyone knew," he said. "I didn't like how he (Cummins) did go at Usman and got personal. I probably get why but I just don't think it needed to happen."

Source: Reuters

FAST

PARIS, Nov 15 : France have recalled flyhalf Matthieu Jalibert to the 42-man squad for Saturday's Nations Championship test against Argentina, which will help ease an injury crisis for the team. Jalibert hurt his quadriceps in French Top 14 rugby in September and suffered a further setback in training last month but has been passed fit to play for France, who employed captain Antoine Dupont at flyhalf and interchanged him with scrumhalf Maxime Lucu as they edged South Africa 21-19 in Paris on Friday. The innovative tactical ploy, which was seen as a gamble but ultimately proved successful, was necessitated by an injury crisis in the pivot position. Jalibert, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy all missed the November tests, and Romain Ntamack dislocated his left shoulder in the first half of the victory over Fiji in Lyon on November 7.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Louise Heavens)

Source: Reuters

item.title: Cuánto cuesta el Huawei Watch D3, el reloj que monitorea la presión arterial con grado médico
item.description: El nuevo smartwatch de la compañía china incluye una bolsa es su correa que se asemeja a un baumanómetro para ofrecer lecturas más precisas vinculadas a la salud.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Garrido
item.content:encoded: El nuevo smartwatch de Huawei Watch D3 anticipa el futuro de los llamados wearables: ofrece conectividad para crear todo un ecosistema con otros dispositivos, pero sobre todo busca ser un asistente de salud de grado médico que se puede llevar en la muñeca. El modelo de la compañía china incorpora una bolsa de aire en la correa, parecida a la que utilizan los baumanómetros tradicionales. Este mecanismo permite realizar un “monitoreo de la presión arterial de grado médico” en distintos escenarios, de acuerdo con el sitio oficial de Huawei. El reloj también permite hacer lecturas relacionadas con los hábitos de sueño y descanso e incluso cuenta con un modo de silla de ruedas para que las personas que son usuarias de este tipo de dispositivos puedan realizar lecturas más precisas. Pero, ¿cuánto cuesta tener un dispositivo de este tipo en la muñeca? Actualmente, el Huawei Watch D3 tiene un precio en México de MXN$6.999 (ya con descuento). Además el sitio oficial ofrece otros cupones adicionales y por el Buen Fin 2026 incluye otros descuentos en plataformas como Mercado Libre. En Chile, el smartwatch cuesta 499.990 pesos chilenos y en Perú se puede adquirir por 1.699 soles. En cada uno de estos países, la compañía también ofrece algunos descuentos. A diferencia de otros relojes inteligentes del mercado que ofrecen mediciones de salud similares, el smartwatch de Huawei no solo se sustenta en sensores ópticos y algoritmos, sino que incorpora un sistema mecánico de medición de presión arterial integrado en la correa. Al inflarse, ejerce presión sobre la muñeca y permite registrar las oscilaciones del flujo sanguíneo. En el caso de parámetros como la oxigenación, el reloj incluso evita hacer muestreo cuando el cuerpo está en movimiento con la finalidad de dar lecturas más precisas, explicó a Bloomberg Línea Iván Martínez, experto de producto para Huawei México. La inteligencia artificial y los algoritmos ayudan a identificar ese tiempo de condiciones y recopilar todos esos datos para una lectura más precisa que se puede visualizar en la app de salud de la compañía. “Va a generar tendencias y entender toda la información que ya recolectó en un día, hace un resumen en la noche y en la mañana siguiente nos dice como está el estado de recuperación física, si hay que tomar lecturas”, precisó Martínez. El experto destacó que instituciones como la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México ya han comenzado a incorporar el relojes y sus mediciones en estudios. El mercado de los smartwatches está experimentando una transformación hacia dispositivos con mayores prestaciones. Counterpoint Research reportó que el precio promedio de venta aumentó 5% en 2025, impulsado por un mayor desarrollo tecnológico como sensores más precisos y herramientas de monitoreo de salud. De acuerdo con Martínez, a diferencia de otros dispositivos que se concentran en monitoreo de mediciones enfocadas a deportes, el Huawei Watch D3 dispositivo está comenzado a atraer a quienes buscan dar un seguimiento integral de la salud. “El consumidor que se está acercando es el que sabe que tiene que tomarse lecturas de presión arterial”, señaló. “Incluso algunas instituciones en el mundo lo utilizan como referente, porque son dispositivos portátiles que van a dar un seguimiento que solo se haría con equipos enormes”

item.title: Noel Tata questions big investments as $185 billion group feud deepens
item.description: Noel Tata has backed investments in strategic sectors but questioned whether projects are being executed with enough discipline ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Shinjini Datta Noel Tata, chairman of the trusts that control Tata Group, questioned whether some of the conglomerate’s biggest investments are being executed with enough discipline, deepening a dispute over capital allocation, control and a potential listing of its holding company. The clash has widened as the group commits billions of dollars to semiconductors, aviation, electronics and electric-vehicle batteries, while the trusts that own 66% of Tata Sons Pvt. resist a listing that would bring outside shareholders into the closely held parent. The dispute now reaches beyond succession and ownership to how a group generating about $185 billion in annual revenue is funded, governed and run. “The question is, do we have the discipline when we execute projects, and not the direction?” Tata said Saturday at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi. “How will projects with a long gestation period succeed if we don’t have discipline?” Much of the expansion has been pursued under Natarajan Chandrasekaran, the professional executive who has led Tata Sons since 2017. A confidential analysis prepared by Tata Trusts and reviewed by Bloomberg News estimated that semiconductors, electronics and aviation would require more than 2 trillion rupees ($21 billion) in additional capital. The governance dispute widened after Tata Sons’ board backed Chandrasekaran for another five-year term on Sept. 17 despite Noel Tata’s opposition. A spokesperson for Tata Sons didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment on his remarks about execution, capital allocation and a possible listing, sent over the weekend. Tata companies generated about $185 billion in revenue in the year through March and own businesses ranging from Jaguar Land Rover to Tetley tea. Tata Trusts owns 66% of Tata Sons, and profits from group companies ultimately help fund philanthropy. That ownership structure has also allowed Tata Sons to support businesses through periods of weak returns or heavy investment. Noel Tata has argued that a public listing, and the arrival of thousands of outside shareholders, could make that model harder to sustain. “My worry is that listing, which is what some people are proposing, will change the Tata way,” he said. With 30,000 to 40,000 shareholders, “profit may take precedence over philanthropy.” Pressure to go public intensified after the Reserve Bank of India classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company, a designation that carries listing requirements. The Trusts have opposed that outcome and explored a restructuring aimed at keeping the parent private. Noel Tata said the Trusts remain “100% behind” investments in projects of national importance, even as he called for greater discipline in how the group executes them and allocates capital.

ASEAN keeps Myanmar restrictions but opens path to political return

In a notable step, the bloc also appeared to endorse bilateral outreach to Myanmar among its member countries.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr (centre) and First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos (right) pose for a photo with Myanmar Director-General of the ASEAN Affairs Department Han Win Aung during the 49th ASEAN Summit on Nov 15, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. (Photo: Reuters)

FAST

MANILA: Southeast Asian leaders said on Sunday (Nov 15) they may consider gradually restoring Myanmar's full political representation in the regional bloc, if the country makes progress on their longstanding plan to resolve its five-year-old crisis. Leaders of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations agreed at a summit in Manila to maintain their policy of excluding Myanmar from full political representation at ASEAN summits and foreign ministers' meetings for now. But they said they had agreed to pursue a "calibrated engagement" through a "phased and progress-based" approach, if Myanmar makes "sustained and concrete" progress on the bloc's proposed plan, known as the five-point consensus, or 5PC.

ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus

Following a 2021 military coup , ASEAN has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings as it has yet to make meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities.  During a meeting in April 2021, all ASEAN leaders reached a consensus about the situation in Myanmar. The five points are: First, there shall be immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar and all parties shall exercise utmost restraint. Second, constructive dialogue among all parties concerned shall commence to seek a peaceful solution in the interests of the people. Third, a special envoy of the ASEAN chair shall facilitate mediation of the dialogue process, with the assistance of the secretary-general of ASEAN. Fourth, ASEAN shall provide humanitarian assistance through the AHA Centre. Fifth, the special envoy and delegation shall visit Myanmar to meet with all parties concerned.

Collapse Expand

And in a notable step, the bloc also appeared to endorse bilateral outreach to Myanmar among its member countries.
